Samir: Quick check-in — ran a run of the continuous-batcher with the new token-budget smoothing (alpha=0.25) + KV warm-prioritization. Saw a weird spike in p95 for small prompts. attaching profiler snippet below.
Samir: ```
2026-05-02T10:41:12Z batcher[pid=42] slot=5 formed_size=12 tokens_total=84 kernel=matmul_opt decode_ms=9.2 kv_lookup_ms=0.8 prefix_hit=0.11
2026-05-02T10:41:13Z runtime[pid=88] decode_ms=1.9 kernel=mv_opt handoff=true
2026-05-02T10:41:13Z batcher[pid=42] admission=delayed reason=token_budget_exhausted queue_len=34
```
Samir: Notably kernel flips to `mv_opt` on the tail which increases variance in decode_ms. Also kv prefix hit dropped to 11% on those intervals.
Jia: Huh. Did you correlate with classifier buckets? small prompts could be mis-classified into the medium decode-rate bin.
Samir: I did. The classifier threshold (len < 48 => short, 48-256 => mid) bumped ~15% of sub-40 prompts into mid after we smoothed token budgets — likely because effective decode_rate estimate uses a rolling window that includes earlier batched long prompts.
Marta: So smoothing made recent long requests bleed into the estimator, raising the predicted decode length for otherwise short prompts. That would cause them to be routed to slab with different kernel.
Ryan: Can you paste the classifier debug output for one of those spans? The one where p95 jumped at 10:41:12.
Samir: ```
[3135012345] classifier: req_id=abc123 len=28 est_decode_rate=1.9 window_samples=20 smoothed_rate=2.1 assigned_bucket=mid
[3135012346] admission: token_budget_remaining=0.03 target_budget=0.08 action=enqueue
[3135012347] runtime: kernel_selected=mv_opt reason=latency_vs_cost tradeoff=latency
```
Jia: ok. So assigned_bucket=mid despite len=28. That explains kernel mismatch.
Marta: Two levers: 1) make classifier rely more on length for sub-64 prompts (hard threshold/hysteresis) 2) reduce smoothing alpha temporarily during high-tail variance windows.
Samir: I prototyped a hysteresis tweak: require two consecutive window ticks to change bucket for lengths <64. Results: drop in misclassification to ~3% in local sim.
Ryan: Nice. What about KV behavior? You mentioned prefix_hit down to 11%.
Samir: kv-prioritization currently uses LRU with incoming weight. At high queue_len, we deprioritize background prefetches to save token budget. That reduced warmups.
Marta: Could we add a tiny prefetch budget reserved for short-prompt cohorts? Like a per-bucket min_prefetch_tokens=0.02 of budget.
Jia: Worth trying. Short prompts benefit heavily from KV hits.
Samir: I ran an A/B: baseline vs hysteresis + per-bucket min_prefetch=0.02. Baseline p95 for short cohort = 72ms, new = 48ms. KV hit improved from 11% -> 36% on short cohort.
Ryan: That's a solid win. Any regressions elsewhere?
Samir: Slight increase in avg for long cohort (+2.4ms) because we shifted some prefetch budget. Overall 99th across all requests unchanged.
Marta: We should also check kernel handoff complexity. If we keep misclassifications low, handoffs drop. But what about when handoffs still happen mid-decode? That flip is expensive.
Jia: I dug into handoff traces — the runtime switches kernels only at decode boundary, but the batcher sometimes groups tokens with mixed kernel affinities and runtime picks the kernel for entire batch based on highest estimate. That causes batches of primarily short prompts to be forced to heavy kernel if one long prompt sneaks in.
Samir: Proposed change: when forming batch, compute weighted-kernel-score; if dominant weight > 0.75 pick its kernel; else split batch into two microbatches at the kernel boundary (cheap to do if combined tokens < threshold).
Ryan: Microbatching could increase scheduling overhead. We need a cost model: extra setup cost vs per-token decode savings.
Samir: I have simple model numbers: setup_ms=0.9, per_token_saved=0.02ms when using faster kernel. For a batch with 120 tokens, if 20 tokens can use faster kernel -> savings 0.4ms net = -0.5ms (i.e., not worth it). But if 60 tokens -> savings 1.2ms net = +0.3ms.
Marta: So threshold around 35-40% dominance. That aligns with Ryan's 0.75 suggestion but we should compute dominance over token-weight not requests.
Jia: Agree token-weighted dominance threshold 0.4. Also add a limit: only microbatch when combined setup cost < 10% of expected decode time to avoid thrash.
Samir: Implementation plan: 
- classifier: add len-based hysteresis for <64 tokens (opt-in flag `classifier.hysteresis_small=true`)
- batcher: token-weighted dominance 0.4, microbatch fallback with setup budget check
- kv: per-bucket min_prefetch_tokens config
- metrics: new labels `misclass_rate.bucket.short`, `kv_hit.bucket.short`, `handoff.count`
Samir: I'll push a canary later today. deploy-bot: starting canary to eng-runtime-canary pool (3 nodes)
deploy-bot: canary started: id=canary-2026-05-02-313501
kv-bot: Prefetch budget set for bucket=short min=0.02 applied on canary
Ryan: After canary, let's run the same microbench harness for 2k requests: 70% short, 20% mid, 10% long. Capture p50/p95/p99 and misclass rates.
Marta: Also log KV prefix heatmap for short cohort. I want to see distribution of prefixes.
Samir: Will post results in this thread. Initial local sim looked promising. :thumbsup:
Jia: Thanks — good to iterate. If the canary looks stable, roll to staging and then dedicated pools.
Samir: ok will follow up with metrics dump.
